nodes.name: Electrochemical Exfoliation of NiPS3
nodes.procedure: The fabrication of NiPS3 crystals was achieved through the conventional chemical vapor transport method (55). Subsequently, an electrochemical workstation (Autolab PGSTAT204) was used to perform electrochemical exfoliation in a two-electrode configuration (Pt wire as the counter electrode and bulk NiPS3 as the working electrode). The electrolytic solution was produced by dissolving 0.05 M tetrabutylammonium tetrafluoroborate (98%) in 30 ml of N,N'-dimethylformamide (99.5%). Throughout the exfoliation procedure, a constant bias voltage of -5 V was applied to the working electrode, resulting in a brown suspension. This suspension was subsequently exposed to an ice bath ultrasonic process at 300 W for 90 min to further disperse the NiPS3 nanosheets. The resulting material was washed with ethanol five times to eliminate the residual exfoliation electrolyte on the surface of nanosheets and then dried under vacuum at 60°C overnight to yield EE-NiPS3 powder.

nodes.name: Ultrafast Fe Doping of NiPS3
nodes.procedure: First, 20 mg of EE-NiPS3 powder was ultrasonically dispersed in 5 ml of deionized water to obtain suspension A. Second, a preheated aqueous solution containing Fe³⁺ ions was prepared: Iron(III) chloride hexahydrate (0.101 g, 0.37 mmol) and sodium nitrate (0.212 g, 2.49 mmol) were dissolved in 45 ml of deionized water and kept at 100°C under the protection of argon for at least 5 min to obtain a deep orange solution B. Then, the preheated suspension A was quickly injected into solution B and kept for 10 s at 100°C. Last, Fe/NiPS3 powder was obtained by washing the product with deionized water/ethanol several times and drying overnight under vacuum at 60°C. The sample prepared with 0.37 mmol of iron(III) chloride hexahydrate and 2.49 mmol of sodium nitrate was named Fe/NiPS3-4.

nodes.description: OER performance in 1 M KOH on glassy carbon electrode (multiple catalysts)
nodes.source_text: After loading on planar glassy carbon electrodes, the OER catalytic properties of different samples were evaluated in a 1 M KOH electrolyte (Fig. 4, A and B). The Fe/NiPS₃-4 catalyst can deliver the OER with low overpotential (η₁₀, at 10mAcm⁻²) of 242mV and a small Tafel slope of 78.1mVdec⁻¹ without Ohmic drop (iR) compensation.

nodes.characterization_summary: AFM test results indicate that the thickness of EE-NiPS₃ is approximately 2.70 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The atomic force microscope test results indicate that the thickness of EE-NiPS₃ is approximately 2.70 nm (fig. S14).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe/NiPS₃ exhibits a notably granular rough surface morphology compared with EE-NiPS₃ nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with EE-NiPS₃ nanosheets, the Fe/NiPS₃ sample exhibits a notably granular rough surface morphology (Fig. 2D and fig. S15D).

nodes.characterization_summary: Aberration-corrected BF-STEM image of Fe/NiPS₃ shows nanosheet morphology well maintained after Fe³⁺-NiPS₃ reaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The aberration-corrected bright-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (BF-STEM) image (Fig. 2E) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) images (fig. S19) of Fe/NiPS₃ also illustrate that the nanosheet morphology is well maintained.

nodes.characterization_summary: HR-TEM images of Fe/NiPS₃ indicate surface reconstruction after Fe introduction with d-spacing of 0.247 nm for the NiPS₃ (131) plane.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution TEM (HR-TEM) images of Fe/NiPS₃ indicate the surface reconstruction after Fe introduction, and the d-spacing of 0.247 nm is recognized for the NiPS₃ (131) plane (Fig. 2F).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern of Fe/NiPS₃ identifies the (131)/(201)/(132)/(331) crystal planes of NiPS₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected area electron diffraction pattern (SAED; Fig. 2G) of Fe/NiPS₃ identifies the (131)/(201)/(132)/(331) crystal planes of NiPS₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: Element mappings confirm the homogeneous Fe/Ni/P/S elemental distribution in the Fe/NiPS₃ nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The element mappings in Fig. 2H and fig. S21 confirm the homogeneous Fe/Ni/P/S elemental distribution in the Fe/NiPS₃ nanosheets.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD patterns of Fe/NiPS show peaks at 13.9°/28.1°/31.0°/36.1°/58.2° corresponding to the (001)/(002)/(130)/(131)/(004) planes of NiPS₃ with no Fe-related peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3A presents the x-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns of bulk NiPS₃, EE-NiPS, and Fe/NiPS samples... For Fe/NiPS, the XRD peaks at 13.9°/28.1°/31.0°/36.1°/58.2° correspond to the (001)/(002)/(130)/(131)/(004) planes of NiPS₃, and no Fe-related peaks can be observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman spectroscopy shows typical E_g/A_{1g} phonon modes with slight redshifts over EE-NiPS for Fe/NiPS₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The structure of Fe/NiPS was further examined by Raman spectroscopy in Fig. 3B and table S1. It shows the typical E_g/A_{1g} phonon modes with slight redshifts over EE-NiPS.

nodes.characterization_summary: FTIR spectra show Fe/NiPS exhibits higher surface O-H vibration intensity and stronger water affinity than EE-NiPS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3C displays the Fourier transform infrared (FTIR) spectra of these samples, in which Fe/NiPS exhibits a higher surface O-H vibration intensity and stronger water affinity than EE-NiPS.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni 2p peak of Fe/NiPS₃ exhibits a shift of approximately -0.23 eV compared to EE-NiPS₃ indicating reduction in Ni valence state; Fe 2p spectrum suggests two kinds of Fe{III} coordination sites.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Their surface states were further investigated by x-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), as shown in Fig. 3 (D and E)... Compared to EE-NiPS, the Ni 2p peak of Fe/NiPS exhibits a shift of approximately -0.23 eV... The Fe 2p spectrum in Fig. 3E also suggests that two kinds of Fe{III} coordination sites were successfully introduced.

nodes.characterization_summary: Slight downshift of XANES edge indicates reduced Ni valence in Fe/NiPS₃ compared to EE-NiPS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 3F shows the Ni K-edge x-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra of Fe/NiPS₃. Compared to EE-NiPS, the slight downshift of the XANES edge indicates the reduced Ni valence in Fe/NiPS₃.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ni-S characteristic peak shifts toward higher R value (2.28 to 2.31 Å) and Ni-Ni peak shows lower R value shift (3.40 to 3.37 Å) in Fe/NiPS₃ compared to EE-NiPS.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform extended Xray absorption fine structure (FT-EXAFS) spectra were further analyzed... Compared to EE-NiPS, the Ni-S characteristic peak shifts toward a higher R value (2.28 to 2.31 Å) in Fe/NiPS₃ while a lower R value shift (3.40 to 3.37 Å) is observed in the Ni-Ni characteristic peak.

nodes.characterization_summary: Edge upshift relative to iron oxides reveals decreased electronic density and increased Fe oxidation state (+3.37) in Fe/NiPS₃.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the Fe K-edge XANES spectrum (Fig. 3H), the edge upshift relative to iron oxides reveals a decrease of electronic density and the increased Fe oxidation state in Fe/NiPS₃... The Fe valence is calculated as high as +3.37 in the Fe/NiPS₃ material.

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe/NiPS₃ shows Fe-S and Fe-Fe coordination environments distinct from pure Fe foil.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Through the comparison of theoretical Fe-doped NiPS₃ crystal structures, it is revealed that the coordination environments of Fe-S and Fe-Fe bonds have been generated in the Fe/NiPS₃ sample (Fig. 3I).

nodes.characterization_summary: Fe/NiPS₃ shows much higher peak intensity than EE-NiPS₃, ascertaining increased unpaired electrons from Fe doping.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Electron spin resonance (ESR) spectroscopy was applied... The Fe/NiPS₃ is observed with much higher peak intensity than that of EE-NiPS₃, ascertaining the active role of Fe doping in the increase of unpaired electrons.

nodes.characterization_summary: Magnetic hysteresis loops show larger slopes for Fe/NiPS₃ and Fe/NiPS₃-A than EE-NiPS₃, indicating enhanced magnetism.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As displayed with magnetic hysteresis loops (Fig. 5B), the slopes of Fe/NiPS₃ and Fe/NiPS₃-A are larger than that of EE-NiPS, indicating the enhanced magnetism.

nodes.characterization_summary: Two quadrupole doublets (D1: MS Fe{III} tetrahedral, D2: HS Fe{III} octahedral) with D1 content increasing from 60.25% to 72.32% after OER.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ⁵⁷Fe Mössbauer spectroscopy was performed... the spectra were fitted with two quadrupole doublets (D1 and D2)... The content of D1 (MS Fe{III}) increased from 60.25 to 72.32% in Fe/NiPS₃ after the OER reaction.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS data indicate the lowest charge transfer resistance R_ct in Fe/NiPS₃ among different samples.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) data in Fig. 4D further indicate the lowest R_ct in Fe/NiPS₃ toward the best electron transfer property among different samples.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double-layer capacitance C_dl of Fe/NiPS₃ is 1.21 mF cm⁻² indicating higher ECSA.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe/NiPS₃ electrocatalyst is also revealed with higher double-layer capacitance (C_dl, 1.21 mF cm⁻²; fig. S32) and an electrochemical active surface area (ECSA) for OER.
